title: Interim HR Solutions in the Netherlands
subtitle: Senior HR cover for a defined period when your Dutch HR function has a gap to bridge.
content:
When Interim HR Cover Becomes Necessary

Interim HR solutions exist to bridge a defined gap. The trigger is almost always one of four events: an HR manager resigns, a key HR person goes on parental or long term sick leave, the Dutch entity grows faster than the HR function can absorb, or a restructuring creates a workload nobody can carry alongside their own job.

What separates interim from other flexible models is shape. An interim engagement is close to full time and it has an end date. You are not buying a permanent hire and you are not buying occasional advice. You are buying continuity for a period you can name.

What an Interim HR Engagement Covers

A properly scoped interim mandate takes over the running of the function, not a selection of tasks:

  • Employment lifecycle: contracts, probation decisions, extensions, chain rule tracking under the ketenregeling, exits and settlement agreements
  • Absence management: the full Wet verbetering Poortwachter timetable, arbodienst liaison and UWV notification at week 42
  • Payroll interface: monthly mutations to your payroll provider, 30% ruling administration, holiday allowance and reservation checks
  • Employee relations: performance cases, grievances, disciplinary matters and pre dismissal files
  • Governance: policy upkeep, CAO application checks, works council or personnel representation obligations

Dutch Specifics That Must Be Handled From Day One

An interim who learns Dutch employment law on your budget is not interim cover, it is a training cost. The non negotiables:

  • Dismissal is not at will. Termination runs through UWV for economic or long term illness grounds, or through the kantonrechter for personal grounds, unless both parties sign a vaststellingsovereenkomst.
  • Notice and transition payment. Statutory notice scales with length of service, and transitievergoeding accrues from the first working day.
  • CAO coverage. A collective agreement can bind you by sector even if you never signed one, overriding your contract on pay scales, notice and working hours.
  • Wet DBA. Enforcement on false self employment resumed in 2025, so contractor populations need reviewing rather than assuming.

How HRhelp Delivers Interim Cover

HRhelp places one named senior consultant, not a rotating pool and not a junior with remote supervision. Every consultant is a native Dutch speaker working fluently in English, which matters when the same person briefs a US or German headquarters in the morning and handles a bedrijfsarts call in the afternoon.

Engagements run on a fixed monthly fee agreed before the start. There is no hourly meter, so a contested dismissal or an unexpected works council request does not produce a surprise invoice. Most mandates run between three and twelve months, with a handover period built into the final weeks so your permanent hire inherits a documented function rather than a mailbox.

Interim, Fractional or Temporary: Which Model Fits

These labels are used loosely in the market, so it is worth being precise:

  • Interim: near full time cover for a finite gap, ending on an event such as a permanent hire starting.
  • Fractional: ongoing part time senior HR, typically one or two days a week, for a company that will not need a full time HR head for years.
  • Temporary: project or peak driven cover, scoped to a deliverable such as a system implementation or a reorganisation.

If the gap has a name and a date, interim is the right model.

title: Fractional HR Solutions in the Netherlands
subtitle: Senior Dutch HR expertise on one or two fixed days a week, without carrying a full time HR head on the payroll.
content:
What Fractional HR Actually Means

Fractional HR is a permanent seat in your business filled on a part time basis. One senior HR consultant works a fixed, recurring share of your week, typically one or two days, and stays in that seat for years rather than months. You get the judgement of an HR director without carrying an HR director on the payroll.

It is deliberately different from interim cover, which fills a defined gap for a finite period at close to full time, and from project support, which ends when the project does. Fractional HR is the standing answer for a Dutch operation that has outgrown the office manager writing contracts on the side, but cannot honestly justify a full time HR lead.

When the Fractional Model Beats a Full Time Hire

Most international employers reach this point somewhere between ten and seventy five employees in the Netherlands. The signals are consistent:

  • Volume without complexity spikes: a few hires, one or two exits and a sickness case per quarter will never fill a full time role, yet every one of those items carries statutory risk.
  • Seniority mismatch: a junior generalist can process administration but cannot advise your country manager on a ketenregeling decision, a works council consultation or a contested dismissal.
  • HQ policy that does not travel: global handbooks written for the US or the UK routinely conflict with Dutch statutory minimums on holiday accrual, notice periods and sick pay.
  • Cost discipline: a full time Dutch HR manager costs roughly 90,000 to 130,000 euro all in, before recruitment fees. A fractional arrangement buys the senior half of that role at a fraction of the commitment.

What Sits Inside the Retainer

A fractional engagement is scoped as a standing set of responsibilities, not an hours bank. In practice it covers:

  • Employment contracts, addenda and fixed term chain tracking, so no contract quietly converts to permanent under the ketenregeling
  • Onboarding, probation decisions, offboarding and the transitievergoeding calculation on exit
  • Absence management under the Wet verbetering poortwachter, coordinating the arbodienst and the UWV milestone calendar
  • Performance management, improvement plans and dossier building to the evidential standard a kantonrechter expects
  • The policy set: staff handbook, leave, expenses, hybrid working and whistleblowing under the Wet bescherming klokkenluiders
  • Pay review cycles, CAO checks and salary benchmarking against the Dutch market

The Dutch Specifics a Fractional Lead Owns

Part time does not mean part responsibility. Dutch obligations do not pause between office days, so they are tracked continuously:

  • CAO applicability: a collective labour agreement can be mandatory for your sector even though you never signed one. Getting this wrong produces retroactive pay and pension claims.
  • Employee representation thresholds: a works council becomes compulsory at fifty employees, and a personeelsvertegenwoordiging can be requested at ten. Both need groundwork well before the threshold is crossed.
  • Wet DBA: contractor classification is being actively enforced again, and misclassified freelancers create payroll tax exposure that lands on the Dutch entity, not on HQ.
  • Dismissal routes: every Dutch exit runs through UWV, the subdistrict court or a negotiated settlement agreement. There is no at will termination.

How HRhelp Structures Fractional HR

You are assigned one named senior consultant, not a rotating pool and not a junior with a supervisor somewhere behind them. Every HRhelp consultant is a native Dutch speaker who works fluently in English and German, so your Amsterdam team and your HQ read exactly the same advice. The engagement runs on a fixed monthly fee agreed before it starts, which means a sudden dismissal case or an unexpected CAO question never produces an unexpected invoice. Days are booked as fixed slots so managers know when their HR lead is in the building, and the time in between is covered by phone and email.

title: Temporary HR Solutions for Projects and Peaks
subtitle: Extra senior HR capacity for a defined project, reorganisation or hiring peak in the Netherlands.
content:
When Temporary HR Support Is the Right Call

Temporary HR is capacity attached to a piece of work with a beginning and an end. Something specific has landed: a payroll migration, a reorganisation, thirty hires in a quarter, a compliance clean up before an audit or due diligence. Your existing team is competent but finite, and the work will be finished long before a permanent hire would clear their notice period.

This is a different problem from bridging a departure, which is interim cover, and from being permanently under weight in HR, which is a fractional arrangement. Temporary support is scoped to the deliverable and it ends when the deliverable does.

The Projects We Are Most Often Called For

  • Contract and policy remediation: harmonising templates after an acquisition, or bringing a set of inherited contracts in line with Dutch law and the applicable CAO.
  • HR system implementation: data cleansing, mapping Dutch specifics such as holiday accrual, ADV hours and the eight per cent vakantiegeld, and writing the process documentation the vendor never provides.
  • Reorganisation and redundancy programmes: preparing the UWV case, selection under the afspiegelingsbeginsel, settlement negotiations and the consultation trail.
  • Compliance clean up: a documented sweep of contracts, working time records, the ketenregeling position, identity and right to work files and Wet DBA exposure ahead of an audit or investor review.
  • Absence backlog: rebuilding poortwachter files that have drifted, before the week eighty eight assessment turns into a loonsanctie.

Reorganisations and Collective Redundancy in Dutch Practice

Restructuring in the Netherlands is procedural, and the procedure is where foreign employers lose time and money:

  • Selection is not discretionary. The afspiegelingsbeginsel dictates who goes, by age bracket and length of service within interchangeable roles. You do not get to keep your favourites.
  • UWV permission is required for redundancy dismissals, and the application must show the business rationale and that redeployment was genuinely explored.
  • Twenty or more dismissals in one region within three months triggers the Wet melding collectief ontslag, with notification to UWV and the trade unions and a one month waiting period.
  • The works council must be consulted under article 25 WOR before the decision is final, not after it has been announced.
  • Transitievergoeding is due from day one of employment, at one third of a month's salary per year of service.

Peaks: Hiring Waves, Onboarding and Year End

Not every temporary need is dramatic. A funding round or a new contract can double your Dutch headcount in a quarter, and the bottleneck is rarely recruitment itself. It is offer letters, contract issue, BSN and right to work checks, pension enrolment inside the scheme's deadline, onboarding logistics and the thirty per cent ruling applications for incoming staff, all landing at once. Temporary HR absorbs that wave so your permanent team keeps running the business as usual rather than dropping it.

How a Temporary Engagement Runs at HRhelp

Every engagement starts with a written scope: the deliverable, the milestones, the end date and a fixed fee. HRhelp does not staff these with juniors, because a reorganisation or a compliance sweep is exactly where inexperience is most expensive. Your consultant is a native Dutch speaker working fluently in English and German, which matters when UWV correspondence and CAO texts are in Dutch but your steering committee is not. Work is documented in your systems as it goes, so when the assignment ends your own team inherits a finished file rather than a dependency.

title: HR Recruitment in the Netherlands
subtitle: Finding the right HR professional for your Dutch entity, and getting the offer and contract right under Dutch law.
content:
What This Service Covers

Two related things. First, recruiting HR professionals for your Dutch entity: HR adviseur, HR business partner, HR manager, payroll and people operations roles. Second, supporting your wider hiring in the Netherlands, which means the employment law, contract structure, offer design and process work that sits around a hire rather than the sourcing of every role.

The distinction is worth being blunt about. HRhelp is not an employer of record and does not payroll your staff on its own entity. It is not a volume staffing agency placing warehouse, sales or engineering headcount. It searches for HR roles, and it makes sure that every hire your Dutch entity makes is contracted correctly.

Why HR Hiring in the Netherlands Is Harder Than It Looks

Foreign employers routinely misjudge this market. Common causes of a failed search:

  • Title inflation: a Dutch HR adviseur is typically an experienced generalist handling cases independently, not a junior. Advertising an adviseur role at coordinator salary produces no serious applicants.
  • Bilingual scarcity: candidates who combine genuine Dutch employment law depth with the English fluency to work with a foreign head office are a small pool, and are rarely on job boards.
  • Sector experience: knowing whether a candidate has run a Poortwachter case to week 104, or negotiated with a works council, matters far more than years in seat.
  • Employer brand gap: a company with no Dutch presence and no local reputation must sell the role harder, particularly against established employers.

Because HRhelp consultants do this work themselves, they can assess a candidate's actual case handling ability rather than matching keywords on a CV.

Getting the Dutch Employment Offer Right

An offer that reads normally elsewhere can create obligations here that are difficult to unwind:

  • Fixed-term chains: under the ketenregeling, a succession of fixed-term contracts converts to permanent employment after three contracts or three years, whichever comes first.
  • Probation limits: no probation period is permitted in a contract of six months or less. One month applies to contracts under two years, two months to longer and indefinite contracts. An invalid clause is simply void.
  • Non-compete clauses: in a fixed-term contract these are only valid with a written, role-specific justification of compelling business interest. Boilerplate clauses fail.
  • Holiday and allowance: a statutory minimum of four times the weekly hours in holiday, plus 8 percent holiday allowance, is the baseline that candidates assume.
  • Expat tax facility: the facility commonly known as the 30 percent ruling reduces to 27 percent for new cases from 2027 and is capped. Candidates relocating will ask, so the offer should state the position accurately rather than promising a benefit.
  • CAO position: if a mandatory sector collective agreement applies, its pay scales and terms override your intended offer.

How the Search Runs

Search is direct and targeted rather than advertising led. Consultants work their own network in the Dutch HR community, approach passive candidates, and screen on real scenarios: how would you handle this sickness case, this reorganisation, this works council consultation. You receive a shortlist with written assessments, not a stack of forwarded CVs.

Pricing is a fixed fee agreed before the search begins. It is not a percentage of salary, which means the incentive is not to push you towards the most expensive candidate, and your finance team can approve a known number.

What Happens After the Offer

A signed contract is not the end of the process for a foreign employer. HRhelp can prepare the Dutch employment contract, register the employee correctly, brief your payroll provider, set up the absence and Arbo arrangements, and hand over a functioning onboarding. For companies still building their Netherlands operation, this work usually sits inside the HR Settlers engagement rather than being bought separately.

title: Interim HR Advisor for Companies in the Netherlands
subtitle: Senior Dutch HR and employment law counsel on call, without adding a permanent role to your structure.
content:
What an Interim HR Advisor Does

An interim HR advisor is senior counsel, not a manager. The advisor does not run your HR function, sit in your org chart, or take responsibility for your team. Instead, the advisor is the person your HR generalist, office manager or country lead calls before a decision becomes expensive: a sickness case that is drifting, a performance file that will not survive a court hearing, a contract clause that quietly binds you for three years.

This model suits companies that already have HR capacity but lack Dutch depth. A capable HR coordinator can run onboarding, absence registration and payroll input perfectly well. What they usually cannot do is judge whether a dismissal file meets the redelijke grond standard, or whether a collective labour agreement applies to your operation by sector rather than by choice.

How Advisory Differs From Interim Management

The distinction matters commercially, because it changes cost and accountability:

  • Interim HR manager: takes ownership of the function, leads people, carries deliverables, typically 3 to 5 days per week.
  • Interim HR advisor: carries no line responsibility, advises named decision makers, typically a set number of hours per month.
  • Interim HR support: hands-on operational execution, administration and case handling.

If your problem is that nobody is steering HR, you need a manager. If your problem is that decisions are being made without Dutch legal judgement behind them, you need an advisor. HRhelp will say plainly which one your situation calls for, including when the honest answer is neither.

The Dutch Questions That Need Senior Judgement

Most advisory work in the Netherlands concentrates in a small number of high consequence areas:

  • Long-term sickness: the Wet verbetering Poortwachter timeline runs 104 weeks. A weak reintegration file at week 88 can trigger a loonsanctie, a further year of salary at the employer's cost.
  • Dismissal routing: redundancy and long-term illness go through the UWV; underperformance and broken working relationships go to the kantonrechter. Choosing the wrong route wastes months.
  • Transition payment: due from day one of employment, including in probation, and payable in most employer-initiated exits.
  • CAO applicability: a sector collective agreement can be mandatory (algemeen verbindend verklaard) whether or not you signed anything. It overrides your handbook on pay scales, notice and allowances.
  • Wet DBA: since enforcement resumed, engaging contractors who work under direction and embedded in your team carries real reclassification and payroll tax exposure.
  • Employee representation: a works council (OR) becomes obligatory at 50 employees, and a personnel representation body can be required from 10.

How the Engagement Is Structured

You get one named senior consultant, not a rotating pool and not a junior with a template library. Advice is given in writing where it needs to be relied on, and by phone where speed matters more than formality. Everything is delivered in English or Dutch, and in German where the parent company needs it.

Pricing is a fixed monthly fee tied to an agreed scope and response time, so finance can forecast it and nobody hesitates to pick up the phone because the meter is running. Where a case escalates beyond HR counsel, HRhelp involves an employment lawyer and stays in the room to translate the legal position into a workable people decision.

When This Is the Wrong Choice

An interim HR advisor is not the answer when there is no one internally to act on the advice. Advisory only works if someone owns execution. If your Netherlands operation has nobody holding HR at all, an outsourced HR department or an embedded interim manager will serve you better, and will usually cost less than advice that never gets implemented.

title: Interim HR Manager for Your Dutch Operation
subtitle: An embedded senior HR manager who leads your Dutch HR function while the role sits vacant.
content:
What an Interim HR Manager Owns

An interim HR manager is not an adviser who visits. The role sits inside your organisation chart, carries decision rights and is accountable for outcomes exactly as a permanent postholder would be. For the Dutch entity of an international group, that usually means owning the local HR function end to end while reporting into a regional or global HR lead abroad.

Typical authority includes signing off offers and contracts within an agreed band, chairing works council or personnel representation meetings, approving reintegration plans, managing any local HR staff, and acting as the escalation point for line managers on people issues.

Why the Dutch Context Changes the Job

A capable HR manager from a common law market can be blindsided here. Three areas cause most of the damage:

  • Termination. There is no unilateral exit route. Economic redundancy and long term illness go to UWV, personal grounds go to the kantonrechter, and both need a dossier built months before the decision. The practical alternative is a negotiated vaststellingsovereenkomst.
  • Illness. The employer carries salary continuation and active reintegration duties for 104 weeks under Wet verbetering Poortwachter. A thin dossier at the week 88 review can trigger a loonsanctie, extending the wage obligation by a further year.
  • Fixed term work. The ketenregeling converts a chain of temporary contracts into permanent employment, and missing the aanzegtermijn on a contract of six months or longer costs one month of pay.

Works Councils and Consultation Duties

Employee representation obligations scale with headcount and are routinely discovered too late:

  • From 50 employees: an ondernemingsraad is mandatory, with advice rights on reorganisations, relocations and major investments, and consent rights on core HR policies including working hours, absence policy and appraisal systems.
  • Between 10 and 49 employees: a personeelsvertegenwoordiging can be required on request, and staff meeting obligations apply.
  • Practical effect: a reorganisation launched without a completed advice procedure can be halted by the Enterprise Chamber, so consultation belongs in the project timetable rather than bolted on at the end.

The First Thirty Days

An interim manager who spends a month observing has burned a quarter of a short mandate. HRhelp consultants work to a fixed opening sequence: an inventory of contracts, policies and open cases in week one, a risk list with named owners by the end of week two, and an action plan agreed with the local managing director and the group HR lead before day thirty. Anything live, an unmanaged sickness case or an expiring fixed term contract, is handled immediately rather than parked in the plan.

Interim Manager, Advisor or Fractional Manager

Choose by the level of ownership you need rather than by hours on a calendar:

  • Interim HR manager: leads the function, holds decision rights, near full time, finite period tied to a permanent hire or a project.
  • Interim HR advisor: senior counsel on policy, cases and compliance without managing the function or the team.
  • Fractional HR manager: the same leadership role on an ongoing part time basis, for a company that will not justify a full time head for some years.

Every HRhelp mandate is one named senior consultant working to a fixed monthly fee, so the cost of the role is known before anyone starts.

title: HR Consultancy for Foreign Companies in the Netherlands
subtitle: One senior Dutch consultant covering employment law, contracts and people operations for your Netherlands operation.
content:
Why Foreign Employers Need Dutch HR Counsel

The Netherlands is easy to enter and difficult to operate in. Registering a BV takes days. Understanding that your first employee triggers a 104-week sickness liability, that dismissal requires prior permission from a state body or a court, and that a sector collective agreement may bind you without your signature, takes considerably longer.

Most foreign companies discover the gap at the worst moment: a first termination, a first long-term illness, a first payroll audit. By then the contract is already signed and the file is already thin. HRhelp works with more than 75 international companies operating in the Netherlands, including LG, Sandvik, Viacom and C.H. Robinson, precisely at this seam between a foreign head office and Dutch employment reality.

Where We Are Usually Brought In

  • Employment contracts: Dutch-compliant templates covering fixed-term chains, valid probation periods, motivated non-compete clauses, notice, holiday and the 8 percent holiday allowance.
  • CAO assessment: establishing whether a mandatory sector collective agreement applies to your activities, and what it overrides in your handbook.
  • Payroll interface: we do not run payroll, we make sure the instructions your payroll provider receives are correct, and that gross to net assumptions in the offer hold.
  • Sickness and reintegration: running the Wet verbetering Poortwachter timeline with the company doctor and the UWV so you do not incur a loonsanctie.
  • Exits and restructuring: choosing between the UWV route and the kantonrechter, building the file, calculating transition payment, and negotiating settlement agreements.
  • Employee representation: works council obligations from 50 employees, personnel representation from 10, and the consultation rights that attach to reorganisation decisions.
  • Contractor risk: assessing Wet DBA exposure where the head office is used to engaging freelancers on terms that read as employment here.

How This Differs From an EOR, a Law Firm or a Payroll Bureau

These are different products and confusing them is expensive:

  • An employer of record holds the employment contract on its own entity. Useful before you incorporate, but it does not advise you, and once you have a Dutch BV it is usually the wrong structure.
  • A law firm answers what is legally defensible, generally once a dispute exists, and bills by the hour.
  • A payroll bureau processes what you instruct. It does not check whether the instruction is compliant.
  • HRhelp is the HR function itself: the party that decides what should happen, documents it properly, and brings in a lawyer when litigation genuinely requires one.

Working With a Head Office Abroad

The hardest part of this work is rarely the Dutch law. It is explaining to a head office why a performance improvement plan that works in Chicago will not carry a Dutch dismissal, or why a global policy update cannot be applied unilaterally to Dutch staff. Consultants are native Dutch speakers who work fluently in English and German, sit in your HQ calls, and present the Dutch position in terms a foreign leadership team can act on.

You get one named consultant throughout, not a ticketing queue. That person knows your CAO position, your contract templates and your open cases, which is what makes advice fast rather than merely correct.

Engagement Models

Scope is set to the stage you are at. Companies entering the market start with HR Settlers, covering entity to first hire. Established operations that need an ongoing HR function use HR Teams. Companies with an existing but drifting HR setup start with HR Reset, an audit and modernisation of what is already there. All of it is priced as a fixed fee against an agreed scope, so a head office finance team can approve a number rather than an estimate.

title: Fractional HR Manager for Your Dutch Operation
subtitle: A part time HR manager who owns and leads your Dutch HR function and reports into your leadership team.
content:
A Role, Not Just Extra Capacity

A fractional HR manager is the person accountable for HR in your Dutch entity, working a defined part of the week. The distinction matters. Advisory support answers the questions you think to ask. A manager owns the function: the calendar, the casework, the manager coaching and the decisions that nobody at HQ has the local knowledge to make.

In practice this means your country lead has one named person to hold responsible for Dutch employment risk, and your line managers have somewhere to go before they say something to an employee that becomes evidence later.

What the Role Actually Owns

The mandate is deliberately broad, because a half owned HR function is worse than none:

  • The employment lifecycle: offer to contract to probation to review to exit, including the transitievergoeding and the correct termination route in each case.
  • Manager capability: coaching line managers through underperformance conversations, sickness reporting and probation decisions so they stop improvising.
  • The HR calendar: pay reviews, holiday accrual and expiry, annual CAO and minimum wage indexation in January and July, pension enrolment deadlines.
  • Casework: long term illness, conflict, restructuring and disciplinary matters, with lawyers instructed only when the case genuinely needs them.
  • Employee voice: preparing for or running the relationship with a personeelsvertegenwoordiging or ondernemingsraad, including the consultation duties under the WOR.
  • Reporting upward: a clear monthly picture for HQ covering headcount, absence, cost and live risk.

Leading Managers You Only See Part of the Week

Being present two days out of five is a design problem, not an excuse. A fractional HR manager solves it structurally: fixed and predictable days so managers plan around them, a published escalation route for the days in between, and decisions documented in your own systems rather than carried in a notebook. Anything time critical under Dutch law, above all a sickness report, is handled the day it happens regardless of the diary.

The Dutch Legal Ground the Role Covers

An HR manager in the Netherlands is expected to be fluent in obligations that have no equivalent in most home markets:

  • Two years of sick pay: the employer carries salary continuation and active reintegration for 104 weeks, and a weak dossier at the UWV assessment triggers a third year.
  • The ketenregeling: after three fixed term contracts or three years, the next contract is permanent by operation of law. The tracking has to be systematic.
  • Dismissal by route: redundancy and long term illness go to UWV, performance and broken relationships go to the kantonrechter, and most cases end in a vaststellingsovereenkomst. Choosing the wrong route wastes months.
  • CAO obligations: a mandatory sector agreement can dictate pay scales, allowances and notice, overriding whatever your contract template says.
  • Wet DBA: long standing contractors doing employee shaped work create retroactive payroll tax and pension liability for the Dutch entity.

How HRhelp Places a Fractional HR Manager

You get one named senior consultant with meaningful Dutch employment law experience, introduced to your team as your HR manager rather than as an outside supplier. HRhelp consultants are native Dutch speakers working fluently in English and German, which matters when a works council meeting runs in Dutch and the minutes have to satisfy a board in another country. Pricing is a fixed monthly fee for an agreed scope and day pattern, so an unexpected restructuring conversation does not arrive as a surprise line on an invoice.

title: Interim HR Support for International Employers
subtitle: Hands-on operational HR help that clears your backlog of contracts, cases and administration.
content:
Operational Support, Not HR Leadership

Interim HR support is the hands on layer of the function. It is the work that keeps an employer compliant and employees paid correctly: contracts drafted and issued, absence files kept current, payroll mutations prepared, onboarding run, employee questions answered. It is deliberately not the strategic layer. If you need someone to lead the function and hold decision rights, that is an interim HR manager, and the two are often deployed together.

Foreign employers usually reach for this when the Dutch entity has grown past the point where an office manager or a finance controller can absorb HR on the side, but has not yet grown enough to justify a permanent HR hire.

What Interim HR Support Typically Handles

  • Contract administration: drafting and issuing Dutch employment contracts, addenda, extensions and probation confirmations
  • Onboarding and offboarding: identity and BSN checks, payroll enrolment, 30% ruling applications, final settlements and holiday balance calculations
  • Absence administration: sickness registration, arbodienst appointments, Poortwachter document deadlines and UWV notifications
  • Payroll preparation: monthly mutations to your payroll provider, verification of the run before payment, holiday allowance and thirteenth month checks
  • Employee questions: a named person staff can ask about leave, pay, parental leave and pension, in English and in Dutch
  • File hygiene: personnel files brought to a standard that survives an audit or a court hearing

The Dutch Administration That Catches Foreign Employers Out

Most of the expensive mistakes we are asked to clean up are administrative rather than strategic:

  • Aanzegtermijn: written notice of continuation or ending is due one month before a fixed term contract of six months or more expires. Missing it costs one month of gross salary.
  • Ketenregeling: three fixed term contracts, or a chain exceeding 36 months, converts to permanent employment automatically. Nobody sends a warning.
  • CAO application: a sector collective agreement can bind you by activity, setting minimum scales, allowances and notice periods that override your template contract.
  • Holiday accrual: statutory days expire six months after the year they were earned, supplementary days after five years, and the two balances must be tracked separately.

Sickness Files and the Poortwachter Clock

Absence administration is where operational HR support pays for itself. From the first sick day the employer is on a 104 week clock with fixed checkpoints: a probleemanalyse by week six, a plan van aanpak by week eight, UWV notification by week 42, evaluations every six weeks, and a WIA application at week 88. UWV then audits the file. If the reintegration effort or the paperwork falls short, the wage payment obligation can be extended by a full additional year. Keeping that dossier current is routine work, but only if somebody owns it.

Scope, Pricing and Escalation

HRhelp scopes interim HR support in day blocks, usually starting at one day a week and scaling with headcount and case volume. You get one named senior consultant rather than a shared service desk, and the fee is fixed monthly. A busy month with three sickness cases and two exits costs the same as a quiet one, which makes the line item predictable for a headquarters budgeting the Dutch entity from abroad.

Because the consultant is senior, escalation is internal. A complex dismissal or a Wet DBA question on your contractor population is handled inside the same engagement, with an employment lawyer brought in only when litigation is genuinely on the table.

title: HR Compliance for the Dutch Entity of a Foreign Company
subtitle: Getting contracts, CAO position, policies and headcount thresholds right before they are tested.
content:
What Compliance Actually Means for a Dutch Entity

A Dutch BV owned by a foreign parent is a full Dutch employer from the day it puts its first person on payroll. Group templates written for the UK, the US or Germany do not transfer. Most Dutch employment law is mandatory (dwingend recht), so an employee cannot validly sign away a protection, even where the contract says otherwise.

The risk is rarely a regulator arriving unannounced. It is the first dispute, sickness case or exit, when the paperwork is tested and found thin. Fixing a baseline costs far less than defending a weak one.

Contracts: The Clauses That Must Be Exactly Right

  • Probation (proeftijd): void on contracts of six months or less, capped at one month for fixed-term contracts under two years and two months for longer or indefinite contracts. An over-long clause is void in full, not reduced to the maximum.
  • Fixed-term chain (ketenregeling): three consecutive contracts across 36 months, after which the relationship converts to indefinite by operation of law.
  • Non-compete and non-solicitation: enforceable only in writing with an adult employee, and inside a fixed-term contract only where the compelling business interest (zwaarwegend bedrijfsbelang) is motivated in the contract itself.
  • Aanzegplicht: fixed-term contracts of six months or more require written confirmation of renewal or expiry at least one month in advance, on penalty of one month of salary.
  • Transparent and predictable conditions: a defined information set must be disclosed, secondary employment cannot be banned without objective justification, and legally mandatory training is free of charge and counts as working time.

The CAO Check Foreign Parents Skip

Around three quarters of Dutch employees sit under a collective labour agreement. Many CAOs are declared generally binding (algemeen verbindend verklaard), meaning they apply because of what your entity does, not because anyone signed them. A CAO can override your contract on pay scales, working hours, overtime, allowances, notice and pension.

The same activity classification drives mandatory sector pension fund membership (bedrijfstakpensioenfonds). Enrolment is retroactive: a fund that identifies you three years late invoices three years of contributions plus interest, and the employee share is rarely recoverable. HRhelp issues a written determination at the start of an engagement, because this is the most expensive item to get wrong.

Registrations, Policies and Records

  • Payroll and tax: KvK registration, a wage tax number, correct handling of the 30% ruling for eligible international hires, and the werkkostenregeling for allowances and benefits.
  • Health and safety: a written risk inventory and evaluation (RI&E) with a plan of action, plus a contracted arbodienst or company doctor.
  • Leave and pay: statutory holiday of four times weekly hours, 8 percent holiday allowance payable by the end of May, and statutory days expiring six months after the accrual year.
  • Data: personnel files under the AVG, with retention limits and a lawful basis for screening and monitoring.
  • Contractors: Wet DBA reclassification exposure, enforced again since 1 January 2025. Long-running consultants on rolling invoices are the usual finding.

Headcount Thresholds That Change Your Obligations

  • 10 to 49 employees: a staff representation body (personeelsvertegenwoordiging) must be set up if a majority of staff ask for one.
  • 50 employees or more: a works council (ondernemingsraad) becomes mandatory under the WOR, with consent rights over working time, absence and pension arrangements and advisory rights over reorganisations. Decisions taken without the required consent or advice can be void.
  • 50 employees or more: an internal reporting procedure is required under the Wet bescherming klokkenluiders.
  • 20 dismissals in three months: collective redundancy rules (WMCO) apply, with notification to UWV and the unions and a one month waiting period.

HRhelp maps these thresholds to your hiring plan so each duty is prepared for, not discovered.

faqs.a: For an entity of up to roughly 50 people, the scan and written findings typically take two to three weeks, with remediated contracts and policies following over the next three to four weeks.

faqs.a: As a cultural document, yes. As a legal one, no. Sections on notice, dismissal, probation, leave, sickness, working hours and monitoring have to be replaced with Dutch provisions, and any applicable CAO takes precedence over both.

faqs.a: Yes. The obligation under the WOR sits with the employer at 50 employees, regardless of whether staff ask. In practice enforcement usually begins with an employee or union request, but decisions taken without required consent can be challenged and reversed.

faqs.a: HR Reset is the broader modernisation of an existing HR function, covering structure, processes and people. This service is the compliance layer inside it: the legal baseline your Dutch entity must be able to evidence.

title: Dutch Labour Law Advice for International Employers
subtitle: Practical HR-side counsel on dismissal, sickness, contracts and restructuring under Dutch law.
content:
The Questions International Employers Actually Ask

The requests that reach us are rarely academic. Can we let this person go, what will it cost, how long will it take, and what happens if they refuse. Dutch law answers those questions differently from almost every other market, because there is no at-will employment and no unilateral route out of a contract without a state body or a signed settlement.

HRhelp provides HR-side counsel: the practical reading of the rules, the commercial options, the file, the paperwork and the conversation itself. We are not a law firm and we say so plainly. Where a matter needs litigation, a formal legal opinion or privilege, we brief a Dutch employment lawyer and stay alongside them to run the HR side.

Dismissal: Three Routes, No Shortcuts

  • UWV: the mandatory route for redundancy on economic grounds and for dismissal after 104 weeks of incapacity. Redundancy selection must follow the reflection principle (afspiegelingsbeginsel), which ranks by age bracket and service within interchangeable roles, so you cannot simply choose who leaves.
  • Kantonrechter: the sub-district court handles personal grounds, principally underperformance (ground d), a damaged working relationship (ground g) and the cumulative ground (i), which can add up to 50 percent extra compensation. An underperformance case needs an evidenced improvement process; a court will refuse one built on a single appraisal.
  • Settlement agreement (vaststellingsovereenkomst): the route behind most Dutch exits. The employee retains a statutory 14 day reflection period that must be stated in the document, and the wording directly affects their entitlement to WW unemployment benefit.

Cost is structured rather than open ended. A transition payment of one third of a month of salary per year of service accrues from the first working day and is also due when a fixed-term contract is simply not renewed. Statutory notice runs from one month to four months by length of service. Seriously culpable conduct by the employer can add a fair compensation (billijke vergoeding) on top of everything else.

Sickness: The Obligation That Surprises Head Office

Sick pay is the most underestimated liability for a foreign parent. From the first day of employment, illness can trigger up to 104 weeks of continued salary at a statutory minimum of 70 percent, with many CAOs requiring 100 percent in the first year. Dismissal during those two years is blocked apart from narrow exceptions.

The Wet verbetering poortwachter imposes a fixed calendar: problem analysis by week six, plan of action by week eight, UWV notification at week 42 and a WIA application around week 88. If UWV judges the reintegration effort insufficient it imposes a wage sanction (loonsanctie) of up to a further 52 weeks of pay. Nearly every sanction traces back to a thin file or absent second track (spoor 2) effort rather than to bad intent.

Contracts, Contractors and Restructuring

  • Clause hygiene: probation and non-compete clauses that exceed statutory limits are void rather than reduced, and a non-compete in a fixed-term contract needs a written business justification inside the contract.
  • Wet DBA: the tax authority resumed enforcement on 1 January 2025. A contractor who works set hours, reports to a manager and cannot send a substitute is an employee in substance, with payroll tax, holiday pay and dismissal protection attached retroactively.
  • Restructuring: a works council must be given advice rights at 50 employees or more, and 20 dismissals within three months in one UWV region triggers the collective redundancy rules with union and UWV notification.
  • Business transfers: on a transfer of undertaking, staff move automatically with terms intact, and dismissal by reason of the transfer is void.

How the Advice Is Delivered

One named senior consultant, reachable directly, with the file read before the call rather than during it. Urgent matters are picked up the same working day through HR S.O.S. Ongoing advisory runs on a fixed monthly fee so a difficult case never comes with a surprise invoice, and you are never handed to a junior halfway through.

process.title: Same Day Briefing
process.desc: We take the facts, the contract, the CAO position and the existing file, then confirm what is actually at stake.

process.title: Options and Cost in Writing
process.desc: Each viable route compared on timeline, likelihood and cost range, including the settlement number a court would anchor to.

process.title: Execution
process.desc: Documentation, the conversation itself, UWV or court filings and settlement drafting, with a lawyer engaged where the matter requires one.

process.title: Close and Prevent
process.desc: Fix the underlying cause: clause updates, appraisal discipline, absence procedure, so the same case does not return next quarter.

pitfalls.title: Assuming a Notice Letter Ends It
pitfalls.desc: Without UWV permission, a court ruling or a signed settlement, a unilateral dismissal is voidable and can leave you paying salary for months of dispute.

pitfalls.title: Acting During Sickness
pitfalls.desc: Employees who report sick are protected from dismissal for two years. Moving against them anyway converts a manageable case into a wage sanction and a compensation claim.

pitfalls.title: Undocumented Underperformance
pitfalls.desc: Dutch courts require a genuine improvement plan with support, time and written evaluations. Retrospective notes written the week before filing carry no weight.

pitfalls.title: Long Running Contractors
pitfalls.desc: A consultant embedded in the team for years is a Wet DBA finding waiting to happen, with retroactive payroll tax and employment protection attached.

faqs.q: Are you lawyers?
faqs.a: No. HRhelp gives HR-side counsel: the practical application of Dutch employment law to your situation, the file, the process and the conversations. Where litigation, privilege or a formal legal opinion is needed, we bring in a Dutch employment lawyer and manage the HR side alongside them.

faqs.q: How quickly can you advise on an urgent case?
faqs.a: Through HR S.O.S. a senior consultant picks up the same working day, reviews the contract and file, and comes back with options rather than a holding response.

faqs.q: Can we dismiss someone for poor performance in the Netherlands?
faqs.a: Yes, but only with an evidenced improvement process: clear expectations, real support, a reasonable period and written evaluations. Without that dossier the sub-district court will refuse the request and you end up settling on worse terms.

faqs.q: What does a typical exit cost us?
faqs.a: The statutory floor is the transition payment at one third of a month per year of service plus notice. Negotiated settlements commonly land above that where the file is weak, which is precisely why the documentation stage decides the number.

faqs.q: How does this differ from your compliance service?
faqs.a: Compliance work builds the baseline your Dutch entity must be able to evidence. This service applies Dutch labour law to live decisions: a dismissal, a sickness case, a restructuring or a contract dispute already in front of you.
